about: A Zork-style start: the white house, kitchen, living room, trap door to a cellar and a troll, with the underground apparently still under construction.

done.why: Every exit past the troll room turned out to be an unfinished dead end with a joke note. I had killed the troll and there was nowhere left to go, so I quit.

moments.note: 'take leaflet' failed with 'can't see any such thing' right after the mailbox revealed one.
Going down shut the trap door behind me, and the cellar is reached without the usual Zork steps.
The sword glowing blue and then brightly, and the troll fight, work as in the classic.
The unfinished passage with the pick and the note 'Back soon. -- The Management.'
The crawlway south ends at a plaque saying excavation is suspended. Every way on is blocked, so the game ran out after about 15 turns.

wished: Somewhere to go after the troll.
A leaflet I could actually take and read.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. Someone has left a pick leaning against the rock, and a note: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: Funny, but it also told me the world was out of content.

lines.line: EXCAVATION SUSPENDED BY ORDER OF THE FROBOZZ MAGIC TUNNELLING COMPANY.
lines.why: A second wall, with the same joke.

fun.why: The familiar opening was fun for a few turns, then it ran out.

engagement.why: I lost interest once all the exits were blocked.

difficulty.why: The troll died in four swings and there were no puzzles to solve.

interestingness.why: It is a familiar Zork opening with a small twist, and it ends quickly.

prose.why: The Zork text is solid and the dead-end notes are witty.
